sashi: Heads up — ran a calibration sweep for fp8 + int4 mixed kernels on the staging runtime. Results are weird: overall quality OK but we're seeing latency regressions on small-batch KV-warmups, especially with per-channel scales and a handful of large outliers.
joel: Can you paste the perf numbers?
sashi: Quick numbers from the smoke run:
- single-token median 12.4ms -> 16.1ms (per-channel fp8, with raw calib)
- p95 moved 18.7ms -> 28.4ms
- seq=32 throughput dropped ~3%
Kernel: mix-kern-v3 (fused-attn + scale-cast path); runtime was doing kernel switches based on scale thresholds.
elaine: Is this KV cache warmup related or purely quant scale noise? :thinking:
sashi: Profiling shows a combo: cold KV hit ratio low -> more small micro-batches -> scale jitter from a few numeric-heavy calibration samples -> runtime flips kernel choice mid-request -> stalls on memcpy/sync. See flamegraph below.
perf-bot: perf-run 2398765450 finished. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/runs/2398765450 :mag:

sashi: Flame snippet and sampling script (short):
```
# sample corpus, biased toward long docs
python sample_calib.py --src web-text-100k --keep 20k --prefer-long
# naive clip: none
```
The sample kept ~0.8% examples with huge numeric arrays.
sam: Which corpus? web-text tends to have numeric outliers. Did you include our chat/eval prompts?
sashi: No, didn't include eval prompt set — just web-text + 2k RE docs.
rada: Per-channel stats will amplify per-head outliers; per-tensor can be quieter but hurts accuracy. Per-channel helped quality but introduces extra convert ops and kernel branches.
joel: We saw per-channel gave better perplexity but slowed kernels because of extra per-channel requantize loops. Need the exact hotspots.
elaine: Could we percentile-clip the calibration ranges (e.g., 99.5th) and re-run? That reduces extreme scales and keeps per-channel benefits.
sam: Suggest two-pass calibration: sample broad -> compute per-channel percentiles -> prune top X% -> recompute scales. Keeps representative distribution but removes tail.
rada: Also seeing runtime thrash: runtime chooses int8-kernel when scale<thresh, fp8 otherwise. Scale jitter near boundary causes kernel switching per-layer token -> huge stalls. Add hysteresis to the kernel decision (e.g., require 3 consecutive ticks to flip) or bucket scales.
joel: Agree on hysteresis + quantile clipping. Also consider a fall-through stable path: if KV cold region (first N tokens) prefer single stable kernel (e.g., int8) to avoid switches.
sashi: I'll run a controlled matrix: A) per-channel raw, B) per-channel clipped at 99.5, C) per-tensor clipped + int4 fallback path. Will collect latency, p95, kernel-switch counts, and perplexity on eval prompts.
elaine: Add seed + fixed sampling so runs are comparable. Also include the eval promptset in the calibration mix (10% samples) so we don't diverge from user workload.
sam: Reminder: if we change calibration corpus we must re-run kernel-selection benchmarking because kernel heuristics were tuned to previous distributions.
perf-bot: queued job 2398765600 for matrix run. ETA ~2h. :hourglass:
rada: Also add logging for kernel_switch events (layer, token_idx) as counters so we can correlate peaks with KV misses.
sashi: Great. I'll push scripts and results to the thread when done. tagging @elaine @joel for script review. Thanks :thumbsup:
joel: +1
elaine: :+1:
sam: good plan
